models.name: Model A: Immersed-Boundary FSI with Anisotropic Hyperelastic Leaflets
models.what_it_computes: Fully coupled 3D fluid–structure interaction of tri-leaflet geometry; predicts diastolic coaptation area, commissural apposition height, and peak leaflet von Mises stress during the cardiac cycle.

models.name: Model B: Partitioned ALE FSI with Thin-Shell Leaflets
models.what_it_computes: Partitioned solver with moving-mesh CFD and nonlinear thin-shell structural model; computes transient orifice dynamics, coaptation line integrity, and membrane stress under pulsatile flow.

models.name: Model C: Weakly Coupled Surrogate (CFD with Prescribed Leaflet Kinematics)
models.what_it_computes: CFD driven by smoothed kinematic waveforms from a separate structural simulation; estimates closing pressure distribution, residual coaptation gap, and stress proxies via inverse loading on the leaflet midsurface.

mechanisms.name: M1: Diastolic Seal Under Quasi-Static Transvalvular Pressure
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Coaptation integrity during diastole governs regurgitation risk; stress concentrations at commissures under sustained pressure inform durability.

mechanisms.name: M2: Peak Systolic Ejection Under Pulsatile Flow
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Rapid opening with high Reynolds number drives transient stress; improper load sharing elevates fatigue susceptibility.

mechanisms.name: M3: Early-Diastolic Closing Transient with Sinus Vortex–Induced Flutter
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady vortices in the sinuses can excite leaflet flutter, altering coaptation and amplifying stress hot-spots during closure.

deviation.detail: Credibility Attainment Index (0–7) reported for each factor, separately for every model × mechanism pair; target attainment ≥5 for intended use.

spans: Bench sinus vortex metrics were within 12% of target but could not be faithfully imposed through kinematic prescription when feedback was absent.

The pulsatile laboratory setup reproduced target waveforms and vortex characteristics within 2.4% in diastolic pressure RMSD, 4.5% in peak flow RMSD, and 12% in sinus swirl metrics, providing a physiologically meaningful reference against which to interpret the three mechanisms.
